blocks.text: 如今为黄仁勋欢呼的人已经寥寥无几。他已离开英伟达，此前他似乎牵涉了两起芯片走私丑闻，并被指有三段婚外情，其中一段的对象据称是一名中国间谍，而与此同时他还在与总统唐纳德·特朗普往来。

blocks.text: 全世界都在关注这场丑闻是否会冲击整个美国AI产业，甚至可能连带动摇股市。这是因为黄仁勋掌舵的不只是首家市值5万亿美元的公司，他更是那位有远见的领导者，掌控着驱动全球AI热潮的必备GPU，而这家公司单凭一己之力就占了标普500指数约6%的权重。而且他从未为卸任做过任何接班安排。

blocks.text: 有人说苹果的史蒂夫·乔布斯打破了CEO的固有模板，但他其实创造了一个属于自己的模板。黄仁勋就是无数效仿他的科技领袖之一：用主题演讲发布产品，选定一件标志性的单品服装（就像乔布斯那件标志性的黑色高领衫），甚至偶尔在演讲结尾抛出“还有一件事”制造惊喜。在新闻编辑部里，我们有时会拿那些乔布斯模仿者开玩笑；其中不少人都是西装革履、刻板拘谨，根本没有那种说服力来撑起这套做派。

blocks.text: 第一次看到黄仁勋把黑色皮衣当成制服穿，我也以为他是在模仿乔布斯。（那件外套并不一直是皮的；更早的版本是一件印着英伟达标志的软壳外套。）后来，即便天气炎热，黄仁勋也坚持穿着外套——我不止一次看到他汗流浃背，却不肯把外套脱下来。与乔布斯不同的是，他还在没有多少新消息可分享的时候，举办过不少场主题演讲；他喜欢把公司过去的成就翻出来讲，仿佛那些都是全新的。

blocks.text: “对接下来一年来说，这是股价冲击，不是业务冲击。路线图和制造计划已经锁定到 2027 年，”Moor Insights & Strategy 的 Pat Moorhead 说。“问题是，这些计划用完之后，英伟达还能不能保持黄仁勋那样的创新节奏。比任何竞争对手的芯片更大的风险，是客户在真空期对冲风险。这就是为什么下一任 CEO 需要技术公信力、一套不依赖单个人的运营模式，以及保护 CUDA 的计划。”

blocks.text: “创始人远见、文化塑造者、领导者、AI 行业代言人等等，这些才是真正的损失。我们不认为战略上会有任何改变，”Creative Strategies 分析师 Ben Bajarin 说。“产品路线图已经确定，并且依然强劲，未来几代产品已经在设计、流片或下单阶段。英伟达仍然是最有能力大规模交付其路线图的公司，因为它花了多年时间锁定背后的供应链，从先进晶圆和 CoWoS 级封装到 HBM 和机架级合作伙伴。这种供应地位不会因为一个人离开而消失。”

blocks.text: HotTech Vision and Analysis 的 Dave Altavilla 表示：“黄仁勋打造了一支才华横溢的团队，拥有深厚的工程人才储备、成熟且资源充足的软件生态，以及稳固的客户关系。他的离开无疑会留下领导力和战略愿景上的空缺，但他帮助建立起来的技术、人才和执行力并不会随之消失。真正的问题在于，他的继任者能否延续同样的长期愿景，以及是否愿意在市场尚未成熟时就提前投入。”

blocks.text: Jon Peddie Research 的 Jon Peddie 表示：“公司内部其实没人真想接他的班，所以只能从外部找人。无论这个人是谁，都不会是黄仁勋，不会有同样的雄心、同样的人脉关系、同样的愿景，也不会有同样敢于下大注、做长期押注的勇气。我们在苹果、AMD、英特尔等公司都见过这种情况。所以在投资者看到一定的稳定性、‘如果……会怎样’的疑问减少之前，股价恐怕还会经历一番震荡。”

blocks.text: 2023 年《纽约客》报道称，随后他又转身把公司押在了 Riva 128 PC 图形加速卡上。这个项目野心极大，他不得不裁掉 Nvidia 约 100 名员工中的一半以上，跳过原型阶段直接投入量产，而等到产品出货时，公司账上的钱只够再发一个月工资。所幸这次赌赢了：短短四个月就卖出一百万块，也为后来的 GeForce GPU 以及与芯片代工厂台积电的长期合作铺平了道路。

blocks.text: 大约八年后，黄仁勋认定，仅做 PC 游戏图形领域的领导者还不够。他告诉播客主持人 Lex Fridman，他把公司的全部毛利都押了上去，要在这些显卡中推出一个没人要求过的新功能：CUDA。它让 GPU 能够用于图形之外的其他类型的计算任务，黄仁勋表示，这使每块 GeForce 显卡的成本增加了 50%。

blocks.text: Some say Apple’s Steve Jobs broke the CEO mold, but he created a mold of his own. Huang was one of countless tech leaders who followed his example by introducing their products in keynote speeches, adopting a single recognizable piece of clothing like Jobs’ trademark black turtleneck, and even occasionally teasing “one more thing” for the surprise at the end of their presentations. In the newsroom, we’d sometimes joke about the Jobs wannabes; many were stiff suits who didn’t have the credibility to pull it off.

blocks.text: I thought Huang might be a Jobs wannabe, too, the first time I saw that he’d adopted a black jacket as his uniform. (It was not always a leather jacket; an earlier version was a Nvidia-branded softshell.) Huang later insisted on wearing a jacket even when the temperature was hot — more than once, I saw him sweat profusely rather than take it off. Unlike Jobs, he also held quite a few keynotes when he didn’t have much news to share; he liked to repeat the company’s previous accomplishments as if they were brand-new.

blocks.text: “This is a stock shock, not a business shock, for the next year. The roadmap and manufacturing are locked in through 2027,” says Pat Moorhead, Moor Insights & Strategy. “The question is whether Nvidia keeps inventing at Jensen’s pace once those plans run out. The bigger risk than any rival chip is customers hedging during a vacuum. blocks.text: Roughly eight years later, Huang decided it wasn’t enough to be the leader in PC gaming graphics alone. He bet the company’s entire gross profit, he told podcaster Lex Fridman, on shipping a new feature inside those graphics cards that no one had asked for: CUDA. It was the ability to use a GPU for other kinds of computing tasks beyond graphics, and Huang said it increased the cost of every GeForce graphics card by 50 percent.

blocks.text: “Huang saw that a GPU was really a parallel computer that happened to render graphics. CUDA turned that insight into a platform, and it’s why NVIDIA was ready when AI arrived,” Mainelli tells me.

blocks.text: It was a bad time for graphics cards to suddenly cost more. When the Great Recession hit in 2007–2009, and Nvidia laptop graphics chips also started failing due to design defects, the company lost 80 percent of its market value.

blocks.text: But Huang believed in CUDA enough to invest even more. “He literally handed out high-end NVIDIA GPUs to researchers at industry conferences, while the company seeded universities like Stanford with hardware to encourage development on its platform,” says Altavilla. And by 2012, Nvidia’s potential for AI had started to emerge.

blocks.text: That’s when University of Toronto researchers used Nvidia GPUs to train a prize-winning image-recognition neural network called AlexNet, which is widely credited for sparking the AI revolution.

blocks.text: Not all of Huang’s visions panned out the way he publicly expected. That AlexNet demo directly led to Huang’s bets on chips for self-driving cars, he said, but he didn’t exactly predict AI — CUDA was instead thought of as better and more affordable supercomputing for researchers and scientists. In 2013, I also wrote about how his grand plan for the future of the company relied heavily on putting Nvidia chips in your phone, which didn’t pan out.

blocks.text: But that bet on ARM-based phone chips did put Nvidia inside every Nintendo Switch and may have helped make future “AI superchips” possible — the latest Nvidia AI server chips have ARM CPU cores. And in 2022, the leaders of the AI revolution launched the most groundbreaking AI tech yet on Nvidia hardware: ChatGPT. Six years earlier, Huang hand-delivered Nvidia’s first purpose-built AI workstation to OpenAI, and by 2022 Microsoft had strung together tens of thousands of Nvidia A100 GPUs to handle the load.

blocks.text: “Every time competitors got close, he moved the fight up a level: the chip, then the server, then networking with the $6.9 billion Mellanox deal, then the full rack, all tied together by CUDA,” says Moorhead. “The speed came from how he ran the company,” he adds. “Decisions that took other companies four weeks took Nvidia four days.”

blocks.text: As Nvidia’s fortunes and profit ballooned — thousands of dollars in pure profit every single second! — and as it became clearer that AI would reshape the world in one way or another, something strange happened. Huang became a celebrity. In summer 2024, The Wall Street Journal and social media chronicled that he received a hero’s welcome in his birthplace of Taiwan. He stopped over and over to sign autographs, including one on a woman’s chest.

blocks.text: In person, at presentations, and in the company’s investor Q&As, I saw the tone shift. People began treating the leather-jacketed man like an actual rockstar instead of a wannabe rockstar, asking for photos and autographs and complimenting him rather than asking tough questions.

blocks.text: It felt like he’d attained Steve Jobs’ infamous “reality distortion field” at last — until he popped that bubble himself with his infidelity.

blocks.text: But one fewer reality distortion field in the world isn’t necessarily a bad thing, and as Apple has shown, a company doesn’t go bust just because its charismatic founder is gone. Tim Cook made Apple the most profitable company in the world. The question now is: who for Nvidia?
